questions.question: If you count 50 plaques from a plate inoculated with 0.1 mL of a 10⁻⁶ dilution, what is the viral titer?
Which of the following is NOT an advantage of the plaque assay?

answers.b: It provides rapid results within minutes
answers.c: It can be used for virus purification
answers.d: It is considered the gold standard for virus quantification

explanations.a: Incorrect. This is a primary benefit.
explanations.b: Correct. Plaque assays are slow and require incubation periods ranging from 2 to 10 days.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Plaques can be picked to isolate clonal viral lineages.
explanations.d: Incorrect. It is the widely accepted gold standard.

questions.question: What happens during the incubation period of a plaque assay?

answers.b: Infected cells lyse and release progeny viruses that infect neighboring cells

explanations.a: Incorrect. Antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses.
explanations.b: Correct. During incubation, the virus replicates inside host cells, lyses them, and spreads locally to neighboring cells, creating plaques.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Viral infection spreads and cells lyse.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The overlay is solid before incubation.

questions.question: Why must the cell monolayer be confluent before adding virus?

answers.b: To ensure plaques form as distinct clear zones
answers.d: To reduce the cost of the assay

explanations.a: Incorrect. Confluence does not prevent contamination.
explanations.b: Correct. A confluent cell layer ensures that plaques can be visualised as clear, open spaces against a continuous sheet of cells.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Cell confluence does not affect intracellular viral replication speed.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Cost is unaffected by confluency.

questions.question: What is the typical incubation time for a plaque assay?

explanations.a: Incorrect. 30 mins to 2 hours is the initial adsorption time, not the plaque development time.
explanations.b: Correct. Incubation requires 2 to 10 days depending on the viral replication speed.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Most viruses take longer than 24 hours to form countable plaques.
explanations.d: Incorrect. While some take 7 days, it varies by virus species.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect plaque morphology?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Viral strain determines replication rate and plaque size.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Different cell lines support different replication speeds.
explanations.c: Correct. The external or internal color of the incubator has no impact on viral biology.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Overlay viscosity directly affects viral spread and plaque size.

questions.question: What is the main disadvantage of the plaque assay compared to molecular methods?

explanations.b: Correct. It requires days to get results, specialized cell culture techniques, and manual counting, unlike rapid PCR assays.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Plaque assays only detect infectious particles.

questions.question: In a plaque assay, what dilution range typically results in countable plaques?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Too few plaques is statistically unreliable.
explanations.b: Correct. 30 to 300 plaques is the standard countable range for most standard culture plates.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 500-1000 leads to overlap (overlapping plaques), making counting impossible.

questions.question: What modification can be used for viruses that don't cause visible cytopathic effects?

explanations.a: Incorrect. High heat kills the host cells.
explanations.b: Correct. Focus-forming assays use antibodies against viral proteins to detect infected clusters before cells actually lyse.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Antibiotics do not help detect viral replication.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Eukaryotic viruses require eukaryotic cell systems.

questions.question: Which quality control measure is essential for accurate plaque assay results?

answers.b: Performing assays in duplicate or triplicate

explanations.a: Incorrect. Expired reagents yield unreliable results.
explanations.b: Correct. Replicates are essential to account for pipetting and biological variations, providing a reliable average.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Plaques take days to develop and cannot be visualised immediately.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The overlay is required to prevent free diffusion of the virus.
